correctness.rationale: For each even integer q>=2 the boundary of x^q+y^q=1 has four order-q axial flat points and strictly positive curvature at other normals. Finite-patch van der Corput gives the uniform Fourier bound O_q(r^{-1-1/q}); Watson endpoint asymptotics give A_q=4q^{1/q}Γ(1+1/q) multiplying r^{-1-1/q} cos(r-π(1+1/q)/2) on axes; stationary phase at any fixed nonaxial normal gives a nonzero r^{-3/2} cosine. Positive mean of cos² establishes divergence at each sharp endpoint, not merely limsup. Squaring and taking the Abelian residue yields p_q A_q²/(2v_q)=4(1+1/q)q^{2/q}Γ(1+2/q) where v_q=4Γ(1+1/q)^2/Γ(1+2/q), p_q=2+2/q. Independently checked q=2 residue 12, q=4 residue 5√π, q=6 and 10 algebraically/numerically; q→∞ limit 4 agrees with the square Fourier transform. The finite diagnostics do not prove the full infinite q or all-direction statement: that rests on the stated uniform oscillatory-integral argument.
residual_risks: The oscillatory-integral proof uses established endpoint and stationary-phase lemmas; finite numerical checks only corroborate and do not establish uniformity in q.
Unindexed classical superellipse Fourier asymptotics could encode the axial constant; exact same normalizations matter.
